newsitem.title: ITALY: RUGBY UNION-WORLD CUP REVENUE EXPECTED TO DOUBLE IN 1999.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WORLD CUP REVENUE EXPECTED TO DOUBLE IN 1999.

text.p: Revenue from the 1999 World Cup is likely to be double that of last year's tournament in South Africa, the International Rugby Football Board (IRFB) was told on Friday.

World Cup chairman Leo Williams, speaking at the opening of the IRFB general meeting, said the next tournament, hosted by Wales, was expected to attract commercial support of 60 million pounds ($94 million).
"This compares favourably with total commercial revenues of about 30 million pounds from the 1995 RWC in South Africa," he said.
IRFB chairman Vernon Pugh said he would be recommending that Argentina, Canada, Italy and Japan be confirmed as full members of the IRFB council.
"We need to stabilise present structures and this removes the uncertainty that currently exists for those four countries," he said.
Pugh said the advent of professionalism must not be allowed to divide the game.
"We must ensure rugby does not become so divided that the top end is totally separated from the game below it," he said.

"What we are now afforded is the opportunity to make a quantum leap in our sport, to move it on to ensure that we go from between six and 10 strong or reasonably strong playing countries to at least 20 with comparable abilities so we can have meaningful competition within broad bands.
"While we all know that part of the game now is and will be maintained as a full-time professional sport, the majority of our participants will be involved for recreation and enjoyment."
